candidate.title: parseRefreshTokenResponse now throws on Zod safeParse failure, turning previously-graceful token refresh degradation into a hard failure
reports: [bug] parserefreshtokenresponse throws new error("invalid refreshed tokens were returned") on parse failure, replacing the previous behavior which logged the zod error and ms response and continued with tokenresponse.success && tokenresponse.data. office365 token responses that previously degraded gracefully (logged, keys updated with whatever parsed) now abort the whole refreshaccesstoken with an unhandled error, breaking booking flows that previously succeeded.

[bug] parserefreshtokenresponse throws a generic error when safeparse fails, but in non-sync mode it receives full typed schemas (e.g. googlecredentialschema) that include fields like refreshtoken — so a partially-populated refresh response that previously failed only the strict parse now either passes the minimum schema (sync mode) or crashes the request with an unhandled error instead of the caller's previous graceful handling (see office365 deleted error-logging branch). zoom and google refresh paths that previously handled safeparse failure inline (zoom's parsedtoken.success check, office365's logged-continue) now throw before that check is reachable, converting degraded-but-logged cases into 500s during booking.

office365 calendarservice removed console.error logging on zod parse failure while parserefreshtokenresponse now throws on schema mismatch, and the throw isn't caught, causing a potential unhandled rejection instead of graceful degradation

[advisory] the iteration silently changed failure semantics for the pre-existing path: the console.error zoderror logging was removed and the code now throws via parserefreshtokenresponse on schema failure, ungated by appcredentialsharingenabled. existing self-hosters who never enable credential sync lose the previous graceful behavior (log and continue with stale-but-usable credentials) and instead get a thrown error on any malformed microsoft token response — an objective change smuggled into the sync pr without being called out for acceptance.

claim_restated: parseRefreshTokenResponse should not throw when Zod safeParse fails; it should return the safeParse result (success=false) so callers can handle refresh-token degradation gracefully.
expected_failure: parseRefreshTokenResponse should degrade gracefully (return safeParse failure) instead of throwing on schema mismatch
